issues.description: Method Stock.getStockIngredients() has different return types in the template and the solution. In the template (src/de/tum/cit/ase/Stock.java) the method is declared to return java.util.List<StockIngredient> (signature at lines 17-19). In the solution (src/de/tum/cit/ase/Stock.java) the method is declared to return StockIngredient[] (signature at lines 14-16). This mismatch is structural: students reading the template may implement or call the method expecting a List while the reference solution and some usage in the repository expect an array, which can lead to compilation errors or confusion about whether to work with arrays or Lists when manipulating stock ingredients.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the return type of Stock.getStockIngredients() consistent across the template, solution, and any tests or documentation. Choose one canonical type (preferably StockIngredient[] here because the rest of the codebase uses arrays for stockIngredients) and update the template method signature and its implementation to return StockIngredient[] (or alternatively update the solution to return List<StockIngredient> and adapt usages). Also update the problem statement/UML or instructor notes to explicitly state which collection type students should use so there is no ambiguity.
